resources.string: Erase ALL wallets on this device?

This permanently deletes EVERY wallet (signing and watch-only), the wallet registry, all tracking data and the PIN history on this device. Funds can only be recovered from each wallet’s recovery phrase or encrypted backup.\n\nType %1$s to confirm.
This wallet was created on a different network than the one recorded on disk (wallet.network is missing or wrong). The PIN was not counted as a failed attempt.
The wallet files could not be read (missing, locked by another process, or damaged). The PIN was not counted as a failed attempt.

This data was written by a newer version of BHODL, which this version cannot open (downgrades are not supported). Update BHODL to the latest version to open it. The PIN was not counted as a failed attempt.

This device can no longer open this data: the secret that BHODL stored in the system keyring is missing (OS reinstall, a different user account, a reset keyring, or files copied from another computer). This is not a wrong PIN, and retrying will not help. Restore the wallet from its recovery phrase or an encrypted backup. The PIN was not counted as a failed attempt.
The system keyring could not be reached (it may be locked, or the unlock prompt was dismissed). Unlock your keyring and try again. The PIN was not checked or counted.
Too many wrong PINs. Wait %1$ds before retrying.
Could not verify the device PIN: %1$s. The PIN was not counted as a failed attempt.
%1$d sat/vB is higher than typical. Double-check the fee tier or your custom rate before sending.
%1$d sat/vB is extreme. This is almost certainly a typo or a bad mempool feed — review carefully before sending.
Wipe stopped: %1$d database file(s) are still in use and could not be deleted. Nothing else was removed, so your wallets are still intact. Close other BHODL windows and retry.
Wipe incomplete: %1$d item(s) could not be deleted (%2$s).
Enter your device PIN to open the wallet registry. This is the PIN you set during the multi-wallet update.
Wrong device PIN. Wait %1$ds before retrying.
Write these 12 words down on paper, in order. They are the only way to restore your wallet if you lose this device.
Type the requested words from the phrase you just wrote down.
Type or paste your 12-word recovery phrase. Words must be lowercase, separated by spaces. We accept 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24 words.
Paste the age-encrypted backup you exported from Settings → Encrypted backup, then type the backup password (NOT your PIN).
Choose what you want to track beyond your Bitcoin.
Stocks, ETFs, commodities. Lot tracking, dual P&L (fiat + BTC), opportunity cost vs HODL.
Category budgets, recurring bills, cash flow forecast, savings/burn/FIRE KPIs.
Target-based goals with progress tracking, sinking funds, sat or fiat denomination.
Real estate, cash, vehicles, debts. Full net-worth breakdown beyond BTC.
Sankey flows, activity scatter, calendar heatmap, YoY comparison, advanced charts.
You can change these anytime from Settings.
Enter your PIN to unlock the wallet.

BHODL now supports multiple wallets — read-only tracking for asset visibility plus one signing wallet at a time. Set a device PIN to protect the wallet list, and confirm your existing PIN to migrate your current wallet.
Recommended: export an encrypted backup first via the previous version of the app. Migration is atomic and reversible, but a fresh backup is the safest insurance.
Wrong wallet PIN. Wait %1$ds before retrying.
Could not sync %1$d wallet(s) — showing cached balances. %2$s

This will permanently delete “%1$s” from the registry and erase its encrypted chain-state file from disk. No signing keys are touched. You can re-add the same xpub later, but the cached transaction history will be re-fetched from scratch.
BHODL is a self-custodial Bitcoin wallet. This is the alpha demo flow.
The PIN unlocks the wallet on this device. Use at least %1$d digits. The PIN never leaves this device.
Show this wallet’s balance & history in the Tracker (xpub-only mirror, no signing PIN needed to view).
%1$d-digit PIN: moderate protection against offline attacks — 8+ digits recommended.
Optional 13th BIP-39 word. Mixed into the seed; without it, even the recovery phrase cannot restore this wallet. Leave blank if you don’t know what this is.
BIP-39 passphrases do not match — open Advanced to fix.
The passphrase unlocks the wallet on this device. Use at least %1$d characters: letters, digits and symbols are allowed, spaces are not. It never leaves this device.
Passphrase is too short (%1$d / %2$d characters minimum).
Passphrase is too long (%1$d / %2$d characters maximum).
Spaces are not allowed in the passphrase.
Use a passphrase instead of a PIN

Your PIN is combined with a secret kept by %1$s, so a copy of the wallet files alone cannot be used to guess it. That secret stays on this computer and this user account: after an OS reinstall or on another machine, restore from your recovery phrase.

No system keyring is available on this device (for example a Linux system without GNOME Keyring or KWallet). Without it, a short PIN could be guessed offline from a copy of the wallet files, so a passphrase of at least %1$d characters is required.
Your wallet registry is locked. Enter your device PIN to open it before creating this wallet.
Open the wallet registry with your device PIN first.
A wallet with this name already exists. Pick a different name.
Use a different PIN per wallet

You set the same PIN for this wallet as your device PIN. For best protection, use a different PIN for each signing wallet:

• The device PIN protects the wallet list, watch-only chain state, and tracking data.
• Each wallet PIN protects the signing key for that wallet only.

With distinct PINs, learning one PIN does not give an attacker access to the other tier. You can change this wallet’s PIN later from Settings.

Adding the watch-only mirror will trigger an Esplora full-scan against a public server WITHOUT Tor. The server will see every receive + change address derived from this wallet’s xpub and most providers log queries.\n\nRecommended: enable Tor in Settings → Tor first. Otherwise tap “Continue without Tor” to proceed.
Add the signing keys for this watch-only wallet. After promotion you can send + sign from it; the wallet’s history and label are preserved.
Seed does not match this wallet. Check the BIP-39 passphrase if you used one.
You set the same PIN for this wallet as your device PIN. For best protection, use a different PIN for each signing wallet. You can change this later from Settings.
Promoting a watch wallet to a signing wallet adds spending keys for it. To prevent an attacker who walked up to an unlocked app from triggering this, confirm with your device PIN first.
These are the first three receive addresses derived from this wallet’s stored descriptor. If they don’t match what you expect, cancel — do NOT enter your seed below.
Type the 12-word BIP-39 mnemonic for this wallet. We derive the xpub locally and verify it matches the stored descriptor before continuing.
Pick a PIN that protects this wallet’s signing keys going forward. It can differ from the device PIN — the security review recommends it does, for tier isolation.
Registry not open. Restart the app.
This xpub is already registered as “%1$s” (signing wallet). Pick a different xpub or remove the existing entry first.
This xpub is already registered as “%1$s” (watch wallet). Pick a different xpub or remove the existing entry first.
Track another wallet’s balance and history by pasting its account xpub. No signing keys are imported — the watch wallet can see addresses and transactions but cannot spend.

You’re about to add a mainnet watch wallet and sync it against a public Esplora server WITHOUT Tor. The server will see every receive + change address derived from your xpub, and most public Esplora providers log queries. The link between your IP, this xpub, and your balance / activity is then permanently in their logs.\n\nRecommended: enable Tor in Settings → Tor before continuing.
